h1: Lock In Your Home’s Summer Exterior Painting Makeover Now

nodes.text: Lock In Your Home’s Summer Exterior Painting Makeover Now

A home’s exterior is about more than just its walls. The trim, siding, shutters, gutters, decks, fascia boards, and more must stand up to the elements all year, too. Eventually, however, battle scars appear in the form of faded colors and chipped paint, calling for a professional paint job.

nodes.text: Your house may need repainting anywhere from every three to 20 years, depending on the materials, the quality of the previous paint job, any existing damage, and Washington’s climate.

nodes.text: Summer and Exterior Painting in Washington

Every summer in Washington, the clouds of spring part ways for sunshine, blue skies, and golden afternoons. By mid-June, the state officially shakes off the rainy season, giving people a much-needed window of good weather! It’s hands-down the time for exterior painting.
nodes.html: Every summer in Washington, the clouds of spring part ways for sunshine, blue skies, and golden afternoons. By mid-June, the state officially shakes off the rainy season, giving people a much-needed window of good weather! It’s hands-down the time for exterior painting.

nodes.text: Warm Weather
A good paint job starts long before the first brushstroke — it begins with prep, which involves the following:
nodes.html: A good paint job starts long before the first brushstroke — it begins with prep, which involves the following:

items.text: Washing: A clean surface is a must for proper paint adhesion, and it reveals any damage. Get rid of dust, mildew, pollen, and other debris.
items.html: Washing: A clean surface is a must for proper paint adhesion, and it reveals any damage. Get rid of dust, mildew, pollen, and other debris.

items.text: Repairing: After cleaning the surface, fix cracks, holes, or rotted wood. The goal is to have a sound structure and a smooth finish.
items.html: Repairing: After cleaning the surface, fix cracks, holes, or rotted wood. The goal is to have a sound structure and a smooth finish.

items.text: Scraping: Scraping removes any loose or peeling paint from the surface using tools like putty knives.
items.html: Scraping: Scraping removes any loose or peeling paint from the surface using tools like putty knives.

items.text: Sanding: Once scraping is complete, sand to even out the surface, feather out rough edges, and roughen glossy areas.
items.html: Sanding: Once scraping is complete, sand to even out the surface, feather out rough edges, and roughen glossy areas.

items.text: Priming: Priming seals porous surfaces, covers repairs, and creates a uniform base for the final coats of paint. Primer also extends the life of your paint job.
items.html: Priming: Priming seals porous surfaces, covers repairs, and creates a uniform base for the final coats of paint. Primer also extends the life of your paint job.

nodes.text: For all these steps to be effective, the surface should be dry. Otherwise, the paint won’t bond and may peel, crack, or blister.
nodes.html: For all these steps to be effective, the surface should be dry. Otherwise, the paint won’t bond and may peel, crack, or blister.

nodes.text: Summer weather then shines, literally and figuratively. It brings just the right warmth to ensure surfaces, primer, and paint are moisture-free. Moreover, painters don’t have to worry about the paint drying too quickly (leaving visible brush marks) or not drying at all!
nodes.html: Summer weather then shines, literally and figuratively. It brings just the right warmth to ensure surfaces, primer, and paint are moisture-free. Moreover, painters don’t have to worry about the paint drying too quickly (leaving visible brush marks) or not drying at all!

nodes.text: Small Chances of Rain
A surprise shower can ruin fresh paint, leave streaks, and drag out the timeline of your project. Fortunately, early to mid-summer in Washington is all about crisp weather!
nodes.html: A surprise shower can ruin fresh paint, leave streaks, and drag out the timeline of your project. Fortunately, early to mid-summer in Washington is all about crisp weather!

nodes.text: Of course, no season is entirely rain-free, but having your project underway during this optimal window lowers the risk of weather-related delays. Experienced crews like EA Pro Painters always watch the forecast closely. Count on us to plan the most workable painting schedule.
nodes.html: Of course, no season is entirely rain-free, but having your project underway during this optimal window lowers the risk of weather-related delays. Experienced crews like EA Pro Painters always watch the forecast closely. Count on us to plan the most workable painting schedule.

nodes.text: Long Days
Summer gives you the gift of extra daylight. With the sun rising early and setting late, painters can work on more square footage in a day, meaning they can finish the project faster.
nodes.html: Summer gives you the gift of extra daylight. With the sun rising early and setting late, painters can work on more square footage in a day, meaning they can finish the project faster.

nodes.text: Natural light is also pivotal to the painting process, allowing for better visibility. You get more accurate color matching and the ability to spot touch-ups or imperfections that artificial lighting might not reveal.
nodes.html: Natural light is also pivotal to the painting process, allowing for better visibility. You get more accurate color matching and the ability to spot touch-ups or imperfections that artificial lighting might not reveal.

nodes.text: Steady Temperatures
Too much variation can prevent paint from curing properly. As such, exterior paint thrives under consistent conditions.
nodes.html: Too much variation can prevent paint from curing properly. As such, exterior paint thrives under consistent conditions.

nodes.text: In summer, you can expect more stable, predictable temperatures than in other seasons, steering clear of durability woes! How does the season in Washington look in degrees?
nodes.html: In summer, you can expect more stable, predictable temperatures than in other seasons, steering clear of durability woes! How does the season in Washington look in degrees?

items.text: Western Washington: Summer temperatures rarely climb above 79°F, with the Pacific Ocean cooling things down.
items.html: Western Washington: Summer temperatures rarely climb above 79°F, with the Pacific Ocean cooling things down.

items.text: Eastern Washington: Higher summer temperatures, usually in the upper 80s to mid-90s, still fall within the paint-friendly range.

nodes.text: Protection From Extreme Heat
nodes.html: Protection From Extreme Heat

nodes.text: Paint is decorative and protective. It becomes a barrier against moisture, UV rays, and pest intrusion when applied correctly. Painting in the summer means you’re giving your house a head start on defense.

nodes.text: A freshly painted exterior also helps regulate indoor temperatures by lessening heat transfer through your walls. That extra insulation? Your respite on late summer’s hottest days! Pull your cooling costs down and keep your household comfortable.

What is summer, if not a time to show off your space? With Washington welcoming millions of tourists annually during this season, curb appeal counts more than ever!
